question: When magnesium is burnt in the presence of air, the product formed is:
solution:
The correct answer is__** magnesium oxide**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **magnesium** is burnt in the presence of air, it reacts with oxygen to form **magnesium oxide (MgO)**. 4
 
• The reaction releases a bright white light and is represented by the equation:
 
 
• ​2Mg+O 2 ​ →2MgO
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Magnesium Carbonate (MgCO₃):
 
 
• Magnesium carbonate is typically found in minerals like magnesite and is formed through reactions with carbon dioxide, not through burning in air.
 
• It is used in products like antacids, chalk for sports, and as a drying agent.
 
 
 
• Magnesium Chloride (MgCl₂):
 
 
• Magnesium chloride is formed when magnesium reacts with hydrochloric acid (HCl), not by burning in air.
 
• It is commonly used for de-icing roads, in magnesium supplements, and in seawater desalination.
 
 
 
• Magnesium Sulphate (MgSO₄):
 
 
• Magnesium sulphate, commonly known as Epsom salt, forms when magnesium reacts with sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄), not through combustion.
 
• It is widely used in agriculture, medicine (as a laxative), and therapeutic baths.​
